column1: # net4sats/installer — PIN MANIFEST (DATA, not code)
# Every upstream ref this repository builds from, and the exact commit each one
# must be. This file is DATA: it is the one place the pinned ref NAMES may
# appear, and the build script READS them from here instead of spelling them.
# scripts/build-pinned-upstream.sh refuses to build if any recorded commit
# disagrees with the remote.
# WHY TAGS AND NOT BRANCHES
#   The upstream PRs behind these pins are open and deliberately NOT merged
#   (operator release freeze: pre-releases are with the review club; merging
#   waits for a release and a clean slate). Those PR BRANCHES are the review
#   vehicle and may be REBASED when the release lands. These TAGS are the
#   dependency and do not move. That separation is the whole point: a rebase of
#   pr/... cannot silently change what this repository builds.
# DO NOT FORCE-PUSH, DELETE OR RE-POINT ONE OF THESE TAGS
#   Moving a pin is a deliberate act. Cut a NEW tag (…-2) and record it here, so
#   an existing build stays reproducible. See docs/PINS.md.
# COLUMNS:  <commit>  <repo>  <tag>  <role>
#   role=base    the newest-base installer pin; composed FIRST
#   role=cherry  an independent installer pin; cherry-picked onto base
#   role=module  a different repository; recorded, never cherry-picked here
# Independence is asserted by the build script in BOTH directions with
# `git merge-base --is-ancestor` — these pins are mutually independent and do
# NOT share a base (comfast descends from 5df4c9c; the other two from 346e473).
# The base row is now installer-comfast-3, which still descends from the
# merge-base b042a23 — see the -2 note and the -3 re-cut note below.
# WHY THE BASE PIN IS SUFFIXED -2 (2026-10-26)
#   The Cashu mint preference hint named a mint vendor and the retired DLEQ
#   keyset-rotation workaround, and deploy step 8b carried the matching comment.
#   That is operator-visible brand copy, so it was fixed UPSTREAM, not here:
#   OpenTollGate/tollgate-installer PR #164 (70ee7fc), which also adds two
#   regression guards. This shell must not patch internal/app/* itself — a
#   patched app tree in the shell IS the maintained-fork drift the shell exists
#   to remove.
#   The fix rides on the BASE pin, re-cut as a NEW tag suffixed -2 (one backport
#   commit, 336f51c, on top of b042a23). The original tag is NOT moved and still
#   resolves to b042a23 in git history; the -2 row is what this shell builds from
#   now.
#   WHY THE BASE AND NOT A CHERRY PIN — measured, twice:
#     §3 derives each pin's range as <tag>^..<tag>, i.e. exactly ONE commit per
#     pin, and it composes the base by CHECKING ITS TREE OUT rather than
#     cherry-picking it. So whatever the base tag points at is carried whole,
#     while a cherry pin contributes only its last commit.
#     (a) Fix commit added on top of a cherry pin (gateway-domain): the pin's own
#         fix below it was not replayed at all. Re-measured before this commit by
#         recreating it — b042a23 + a72a4f6..<gw-top> — and the result still
#         contains `gatewaydomainname='tollgate.lan'` (grep -c => 1, want 0).
#         §4 catches it.
#     (b) The same backport given to a second cherry pin: once the first
#         cherry-pick already carries it, the second is an EMPTY cherry-pick
#         ("The previous cherry-pick is now empty ... nothing to commit"), which
#         stops the composition just as a conflict would. Either way §3 refuses.
#   On the base, the backport is carried whole and no later cherry-pick can drop
#   it. Nothing else about the pins changes.
# WHY THE BASE PIN IS NOW SUFFIXED -3 (2026-10-26)
#   §6 of scripts/build-pinned-upstream.sh compares THREE launcher digests — the
#   launcher inside the composed pinned tree, the one recorded in
#   scripts/upstream-launcher.sha256, and vendor/upstream-install-and-test.sh —
#   and it FAILED on -2: the pinned tree carried 7cd397a4… while the shell had
#   recorded 6595640e….
#   The shell had vendored the busybox-`tr` launcher fix itself in 93a0ce4
#   (2026-10-20), because at the time upstream had not shipped it. Upstream then
#   shipped the same fix separately as 298c8d2 (#154, 2026-10-24) — AFTER every
#   net4sats-pin/* tag had been cut, so no pin could contain it. The two copies
#   differ: the shell's in-tree launcher and upstream's have distinct comments,
#   so their digests can never agree, and the shell cannot vendor "the pinned
#   tree's launcher" without taking upstream's bytes verbatim.
#   So this re-cut folds 298c8d2 into the BASE pin: -3 is 336f51c + one
#   cherry-pick of 298c8d2 (9efbd13), touching install-and-test.sh and
#   tests/shell/test-launcher-platform-detection.sh only. Its launcher hashes to
#   4e97751a…, and THAT is what scripts/upstream-launcher.sha256 and vendor/ now
#   record. -2 and the original tag are NOT moved.
#   Nothing else about the pins changes: -3 still descends from b042a23 via
#   336f51c, so it is still independent of the two cherry pins, and it still
#   carries the brand-neutral mint copy and its guards.
